title: Moreton Bay Fig: Giant Fig Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: The Australian giant whose roots arrive before the trunk does. The biggest Moreton Bay figs mapped so far, plaza-sized canopies in mild coastal cities.
intro: A Moreton Bay fig announces itself at ground level first: buttress roots the height of a person come snaking across the earth like walls, and the trunk they support looks less grown than poured. In its native eastern Australia the species often starts life as a strangler high in another tree, sends roots down, and eventually stands on its own; planted in the mild coastal cities of Europe and beyond in the 19th century, it skipped the strangling and went straight to the monumental, single trees shading entire plazas within a human lifetime. It needs frost-free air, which is why every great specimen marks a mild microclimate. The Moreton Bay figs mapped so far are listed largest and oldest first.
